meaning: Troubling or worrying someone again and again; also complaining to someone repeatedly
trick: NAG-NAG-NAG: a thought that keeps poking you again and again.
examples: Then I asked them the question that was most nagging me.
A small doubt kept nagging me all day.

usage.pattern: something is nagging someone / a nagging + doubt/feeling

meaning: Fastened in place with nails; also (informal) done something perfectly
trick: NAILED = hammered NAILS in: the carpet won't move now.
examples: The stairs were covered with carpet, nailed down at the base of each step.
He nailed the picture frame to the wall.

usage.pattern: nail something down / nail something to something

meaning: A person or thing that has the same name as another, or is named after them
hindi: हमनाम, जिसके नाम पर नाम रखा गया
trick: NAME + SAKE: named for the SAKE of someone else.
examples: A whale had swallowed the boy's namesake prophet in the Koran.
My little cousin is my namesake; he was named after me.

usage.pattern: someone's namesake / be named after a namesake

meaning: The back of the neck
trick: NAPE sounds like NAP: when you nap, your NAPE rests on the pillow.
examples: She kissed the nape of his neck.
The cold wind hit the nape of my neck.

usage.pattern: the nape of someone's neck

meaning: Too interested in oneself and one's own importance
trick: NARCISSUS fell in love with his own reflection in the water.
examples: Entitlement closes in upon itself in a kind of narcissistic bubble.
He is so narcissistic that he talks only about himself.

usage.pattern: be narcissistic / a narcissistic + person/behaviour

meaning: Sounding as if the air is coming through the nose; also connected with the nose
hindi: नाक से निकलती, नकियाती; नाक का
trick: NASAL = NOSE-al: a voice that comes out of the nose.
examples: From a cassette player, a man's nasal voice chanted verses from the Koran.
He has a cold, so his voice sounds nasal.

usage.pattern: a nasal + voice/sound

meaning: Feeling as if one is about to vomit
trick: NAUSEA + TED: Ted felt NAUSEA on the boat.
examples: She sat on the bed, missing her mother, feeling nauseated and homesick.
The bumpy bus ride left me nauseated.

usage.pattern: feel nauseated / be nauseated by something

meaning: The small hollow in the middle of the stomach; belly button
trick: NAVEL sounds like NAVAL, but it's the button in the middle of your belly.
examples: He was an old man with a white beard that dropped to his navel.
The baby's navel healed a week after birth.

usage.pattern: someone's navel / down to the navel

meaning: A long strip of cloth worn around the neck under a shirt collar, knotted at the front
trick: NECK + TIE: the thing you TIE around your NECK.
examples: He walked through the tall grass, the breeze lifting his red necktie.
Dad wears a necktie to the office every day.

usage.pattern: wear a necktie / knot a necktie

meaning: Denied or gave up something, so it no longer has any effect; also cancelled out the effect of something
trick: NEGATIVE: NEGATED = made it zero, turned it negative.
examples: Once you have negated your own deep purpose, everybody tests you.
The extra cost negated all the savings we made.

usage.pattern: negate something / something negated by something

meaning: Failure to give someone or something the care they need; also (verb) to fail to look after
trick: NEG (not) + LECT (choose): not choosing to care.
examples: Nobody makes it through life without scars, whether from neglect, loss, or illness.
The old house fell apart after years of neglect.

usage.pattern: suffer from neglect / neglect of something

meaning: Failure to take proper care in doing something
trick: NEGLIGENCE = NEGLECT + ence: neglecting your duty.
examples: Her forgotten invitation is now seen not as an innocent mistake but as horrible negligence.
The accident was caused by the driver's negligence.

usage.pattern: negligence by someone / negligence in doing something

meaning: The loud, high sound a horse makes
trick: NEIGH-NEIGH: the sound a horse makes, like 'nay'.
examples: The terrified neighing of a horse sounded from the yard.
We heard the neighing of horses from the stable.

usage.pattern: the neighing of a horse / a horse is neighing

meaning: A person who is new to a skill, job or activity
trick: NEO = new + PHYTE = plant: a newly planted person.
examples: You'll learn to avoid the assumptions that blind neophyte negotiators.
As a neophyte cook, I burnt the rice twice.

usage.pattern: a neophyte + noun / a neophyte in something

meaning: Unfairly giving jobs or favours to one's own relatives or friends
trick: NEPOTISM = NEPHEW-ism: giving the job to your nephew.
examples: The era of aristocracy, nepotism, and inequality is over.
People accused the manager of nepotism when he hired his son.

usage.pattern: accuse someone of nepotism / nepotism in something

meaning: Settled into a warm, comfortable, protected position
trick: NEST-led: like baby birds settling into a NEST.
examples: The ducklings nestled down inside it and promptly fell asleep.
The kitten nestled against its mother.

usage.pattern: nestle down / nestle against or into something

meaning: Causing annoyance or difficulty
trick: NETTLE = a stinging plant: a NETTLESOME problem keeps stinging you.
examples: People used these tools to work out nettlesome problems at home.
Fixing the leaky tap was a nettlesome job.

usage.pattern: a nettlesome + problem/issue

meaning: A personality trait of being easily worried, anxious or upset
trick: NEURO = nerves: having nervous, jumpy nerves all the time.
examples: It leads to a life of insecurity, neuroticism, and emotional repression.
His neuroticism made him check the lock five times.

usage.pattern: a sign of neuroticism / high in neuroticism

meaning: Taking small, gentle bites of something
trick: NIBBLE = a tiny bite, like a NIBBle of a biscuit.
examples: She batted at the mosquitoes nibbling on her arms.
The rabbit was nibbling a carrot.

usage.pattern: nibble (on/at) something

meaning: Small polite or formal details of behaviour; also fine details
trick: NICE-ties: the NICE little things people say to be polite.
examples: Gone are the fake niceties and verbal webs of politeness.
She skipped the niceties and got straight to the point.

usage.pattern: observe/skip the niceties / the niceties of something

meaning: A small hollow space in a wall or rock; also a special area or market that suits someone
trick: NICHE sounds like 'nitch': a little NOOK cut into a wall.
examples: There's a niche over here where we can look out.
A small statue stood in a niche in the temple wall.

usage.pattern: a niche in something / find one's niche

meaning: Made a small cut on something by accident; also (British informal) stole
hindi: हल्का कट गया, खरोंच लगी; (बोलचाल) चुरा लिया
trick: NICK = a tiny cut; NICKED yourself while shaving.
examples: She pictured telling him when he nicked himself while shaving.
I nicked my finger while cutting onions.

usage.pattern: nick oneself / nick something on something

meaning: US or Canadian coins worth five cents
trick: NICKEL is the metal; the five-cent coin is named after it.
examples: I stored them in a bottle like so many nickels.
He paid for the candy with three nickels.

usage.pattern: a handful of nickels / pay in nickels

meaning: A deeply offensive racial slur used against Black people; recognise it when reading, but never use it
trick: Learn to recognise it in books; it is one of the most hurtful words in English, so never say it.
examples: In his memoir, he says bullies called him nigger, a racist slur that hurt him deeply.
Teachers explained why the slur nigger is so hurtful and should never be used.

usage.pattern: (do not use; recognise only)

meaning: The time in the evening when it becomes dark
trick: NIGHT + FALL: when night falls.
examples: With the two o'clock bus I should get there well before nightfall.
We must reach the village before nightfall.

usage.pattern: before/after/at nightfall

meaning: Quick and light in movement; also quick-thinking
trick: NIMBLE sounds like THIMBLE: you need NIMBLE fingers to sew.
examples: Squealer was a small fat pig with twinkling eyes and nimble movements.
The nimble cat jumped onto the wall.

usage.pattern: be nimble / nimble + fingers/feet

meaning: Happening or active during the night
hindi: रात का, रात में होने वाला
trick: NOCTURNAL: NOCT = night (like 'nocturne', a night song).
examples: On one of his nocturnal visits, Snowball had mixed weed seeds with the seed corn.
Owls are nocturnal birds.

usage.pattern: nocturnal + noun / be nocturnal

meaning: A person who keeps moving from place to place without a fixed home
trick: NO MAD-house: a nomad has NO fixed house.
examples: It was the digital nomad dream, exactly what I wanted out of life.
He lived like a nomad, moving to a new city every year.

usage.pattern: live like a nomad / a nomad + noun

meaning: Calm and relaxed, seeming not to care or worry
trick: NON + CHALANT (heat): no heat, totally cool about it.
examples: He was nonchalant about the whole thing, drawing whatever amused him.
She looked nonchalant even before the big exam.

usage.pattern: be nonchalant about something

meaning: In spite of that; however
trick: NONE + THE + LESS: none the less true for that.
examples: But we all must suffer nonetheless.
It was raining; nonetheless, we went for a walk.

usage.pattern: ..., nonetheless / nonetheless, + clause

meaning: Making no sense; silly or foolish
trick: NON-SENSE-ical: no sense at all.
examples: I knew it sounded nonsensical, and I heard people tittering.
His excuse was completely nonsensical.

usage.pattern: be nonsensical / a nonsensical + idea/answer

meaning: A loop of rope with a knot that tightens when pulled; also something that traps or restricts
trick: NOOSE sounds like LOOSE: a loop that gets tight, not loose.
examples: The cowboy threw a noose over the calf's head.
He tied a noose at the end of the rope to lift the bucket.

usage.pattern: a noose around something / the noose tightens

meaning: Too interested in other people's private matters
hindi: ताक-झाँक करने वाला, दूसरों के मामलों में दखल देने वाला
trick: NOSY = pokes her NOSE into everything.
examples: She's a nosy gossiper, that one.
Our nosy neighbour always asks where we are going.

usage.pattern: be nosy (about something)

meaning: A level or degree on a scale; also a small V-shaped cut
trick: NOTCH = the cuts on a belt: move up or down a NOTCH.
examples: Somebody is jealous and trying to bring them down a notch.
That experience kicked my anxiety up several notches.

usage.pattern: take/bring someone down a notch / up a notch

meaning: An idea or belief about something
trick: NOTION is related to NOTE: an idea you have noted in your mind.
examples: The notion that we would ever run out of money sounded ludicrous.
I had no notion of how hard the job would be.

usage.pattern: the notion that ... / a notion of something

meaning: Ideas or beliefs about something
trick: NOTIONS = NOTES in your head: ideas.
examples: Their techniques had to do with logic and rational notions of value.
He has old-fashioned notions about how girls should behave.

usage.pattern: notions of/about something

meaning: Chewy sweets made from sugar or honey with nuts
trick: NOUGAT = NUT + GOT: a chewy sweet that has got nuts.
examples: A little boy places before them green tea and pistachio nougats.
We bought a box of almond nougats at the market.

usage.pattern: a box of nougats / pistachio nougats

meaning: Gave someone strength, comfort or hope; also fed with healthy food
trick: NOURISH = NURSE: it fed and nursed my spirit.
examples: The way he spun hopelessness into rage nourished me.
Her kind words nourished my confidence.

usage.pattern: something nourished someone / be well nourished

meaning: Giving strength and health; also (of food) healthy and filling
trick: NOURISHING = NOURISHES you: gives you fresh strength.
examples: I waited until I could score one deep, nourishing breath.
Grandma made a hot, nourishing soup.

usage.pattern: a nourishing + meal/breath/drink

meaning: Sometimes, but not often or regularly
trick: NOW ... and THEN again later: it happens once in a while.
examples: The only sound came only now and then, and at first I was puzzled by it.
We still meet for coffee now and then.

usage.pattern: do something (every) now and then

meaning: Very small differences in meaning, feeling or quality
trick: NUANCES = NEW ANSWERS hidden in the small details.
examples: There was no point in teaching sheep the nuances of wolf recognition.
A good translator understands the nuances of both languages.

usage.pattern: the nuances of something

meaning: A small worn-down end or lump; also the central point of a matter
trick: NUB rhymes with STUB: worn down to a tiny stub.
examples: Mentally, I was worn to the nub.
The pencil was worn down to a nub.

usage.pattern: worn (down) to the nub / the nub of something

meaning: Small lumps of gold; also small valuable bits of information
hindi: सोने के डले; काम की बातें
trick: NUGGETS of gold, like chicken NUGGETS: small lumps.
examples: Society expects you to be perfect and produce gold nuggets before breakfast.
Her talk was full of useful nuggets of advice.

usage.pattern: gold nuggets / nuggets of something

meaning: Unable to feel anything, physically or emotionally
trick: NUMB: the B is silent, just like your numb fingers.
examples: "A what?" she said through suddenly numb lips.
My fingers went numb in the cold.

usage.pattern: go numb / be numb with something

meaning: Taking care of an injury or illness so it gets better; also working as a nurse
hindi: इलाज करते हुए, सहलाते हुए; नर्सिंग
trick: NURSING = acting like a NURSE for your own injury.
examples: Nursing a wounded knee, I could barely swim through the waves.
He stayed home, nursing a bad cold.

usage.pattern: nurse an injury / be nursing something

meaning: (informal) Crazy or foolish; also tasting of nuts
trick: NUTTY = a little NUTS (crazy).
examples: Shakespeare wanted to show how absolutely nutty romance was.
My uncle has some nutty ideas about saving money.

usage.pattern: be nutty / a nutty + idea/person

meaning: Pressed or rubbed gently against something, often for comfort or warmth
trick: NUZZLE = NOSE + snuggle: push your nose in gently.
examples: His chin nuzzled into his breast, he slipped through the glass doors.
The puppy nuzzled against my hand.

usage.pattern: nuzzle (into/against) something
